hook: On 21 October 1966 at approximately 9.15am, a towering black mountain of waste buried Aberfan in seconds.

sections.voiceover: On 21 October 1966 at approximately 9.15am, a towering black mountain of waste buried Aberfan in seconds.
sections.visual_cue: Archive photograph showing the black coal tip slide descending toward the village.
sections.sfx_cue: Low heavy rumble building abruptly and cutting off.
b_roll: Historical archival photograph of Merthyr Vale Colliery waste tip
sections.animation_cue: Slow cinematic zoom in on the disaster aftermath zone.

sections.voiceover: Merthyr Vale Colliery sent thousands of tons of slurry crashing straight down onto Pantglas School.
sections.visual_cue: Archival footage panning across ruined school buildings with rescue workers.
sections.animation_cue: Slide right transition into documentary archive view.

sections.voiceover: Yet 60 years later, communities gathered in Aberfan to observe a solemn moment of silence.
sections.visual_cue: Modern documentary footage showing villagers standing in silence.
b_roll: Aberfan memorial gathering and wreath laying
sections.animation_cue: Subtle pulse zoom on memorial plaque.

sections.voiceover: BBC Cymru Wales announced a comprehensive season of programming for the 60 years anniversary. A total of 144 lives were lost when the Aberfan coal tip collapsed.
sections.visual_cue: Close up archival recording log document and contemporary memorial flowers.
sections.sfx_cue: Warm acoustic guitar undertone supporting narration.
b_roll: BBC Cymru Wales broadcasting archive documentary reel
sections.animation_cue: Gentle pan left across memorial names.

sections.voiceover: The total count of 144 lives lost remains forever marked in the village.
sections.visual_cue: Wide cinematic shot of the Aberfan valley memorial landscape today.
sections.animation_cue: Slow fade out to black screen.
